Transport Minister Steffen Bilger, speaking at a Tagesspiegel Background conference in Berlin, said he will work to ensure "Tesla FSD Supervised" reaches drivers in the European Union soon, noting that Germany should seek its own approval route if talks with the bloc fail.

Bilger believes the system can make roads safer and stated his desire to support innovation. This move coincides with an impending EU vote on the technology, and Elon Musk responded to the endorsement on social media by thanking the German minister.

items.title: Michael Burry Warns $573B AI Finance Loop Mirrors 2000 Bust
items.summary:
A network of eight technology firms is using cross company loans and debt guarantees to sustain the current AI expansion, according to Michael Burry. Citing a report from lender Ares, Burry stated that $573B in financing over the last 12 months flows between Meta, Nvidia, Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Broadcom. He warns that these firms buy from and back one another in a circular financing cycle that depends entirely on AI spending remaining constant.

Burry compared this structure to the financing that led to the 2000 telecom bubble and believes the current stock market is in a stage of 'denial.' He noted that this phase historically lasts 6 to 9 months, as observed during the 2000 and 2008 crises, and argues the 'mother of all crashes' is imminent despite the S&P 500 reaching new all time highs.

items.title: Apple Adds Mac Privacy Protections After Meta Muse AI Accusations

Meta's Muse AI agent faces allegations of accessing private messages without user consent, sparking a move by Apple to restrict system permissions for macOS. The company is introducing new controls for the "Full Disk Access" permission to prevent autonomous AI tools from gaining unrestrained entry to sensitive information, including personal files, email accounts, and browsing histories.

Apple warned that the evolving capabilities of third-party AI agents have increased the risks associated with broad system access. These updated privacy protections aim to create more granular boundaries, limiting the amount of data exposed to software that can act independently across the operating system. The changes appear as part of a broader security push for the upcoming macOS updates.

items.title: Math Researchers Abandon Openness After OpenAI's 700 Paper Release
items.summary:
Hugo Duminil-Copin says mathematicians may stop sharing research problems publicly to keep their work from being solved by artificial intelligence. The Fields medallist stated that the current climate of AI-generated solutions on open problems has discouraged the usual openness of the discipline. This shift has reached Northwestern University, where some students are questioning whether to remain in the field, prompting professor Antonio Auffinger to focus on talent retention.

The reaction follows OpenAI's release of more than 700 mathematical manuscripts, including work on 16 problems Duminil-Copin was researching. To manage the rollout, OpenAI created the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI) as a bridge to the community, though AGMAI later clarified that its advisory role was not an endorsement of OpenAI's processes or a judgment of the published results' impact.

items.title: KOSPI Ends Week Down 14.5% in Worst Performance Since October 2008
items.summary:
Asian equity markets saw a partial recovery on Friday, though semiconductor stocks remained volatile following a historic rout in South Korea. The KOSPI index ended the week down 14.5%, its steepest weekly decline since the 2008 financial crisis, and now sits roughly 40% below its June highs. This collapse was highlighted by a Thursday crash of over 8%, which triggered circuit breakers for both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ and halted trading for 20 minutes. Samsung and SK Hynix led the losses as foreign investors sold $3.6B in equities amid fears of a memory chip oversupply by 2028 and a US September CPI print of 3.7% that increased the likelihood of Fed rate hikes.

The downturn extended beyond chipmakers into the broader AI infrastructure trade, with stocks such as Eugene Technology falling 16.5% on concerns over AI capex returns. South Korea's financial regulator held emergency meetings to stabilize the market, while President Lee Jae-myung issued public appeals for suicide prevention following the crash. While Japan's Nikkei surged 2% on Friday to add $150B in market value as Wall Street rebounded, Nasdaq 100 futures edged lower on persistent concerns regarding debt risks at CoreWeave.

items.title: Newsom Bans AI Emotion Tracking and Sole AI Firing Decisions

The state of California on September 30 adopted regulations that block the use of neural sensors and employee sentiment analysis in professional environments. Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order and AB 1883 to prohibit the use of artificial intelligence for reading workers' emotions or conducting terminations without human oversight. Under the new rules, employers must disclose if a mass layoff or relocation is caused by an AI system and are forbidden from using software to exclusively handle discipline or firing decisions.

These curbs come as a counter-strike to a federal mandate from President Trump, who signed an order on September 29 requiring all federal agencies to replace the term "Artificial Intelligence" with "Super Intelligence" or "SI." Trump argued that "artificial" is a fake term and suggested that the industry should rely on self-regulation rather than binding federal rules. The rebranding triggered a land grab for Slovenia's ".si" web domains, which saw over 6,000 registrations in two days and generated millions of dollars in turnover for speculators.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
items.summary: AI leaders joined whistleblowers and security leaders at a sweeping parliamentary session, while a few hundred meters away Britain’s spy chief warned AI could be used to create new bioweapons.
